newsitem.title: UK: Gold prices edge up, but gains seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Gold prices edge up, but gains seen limited.

text.p: Gold prices were firmer on Tuesday following gains overnight, but trade was quiet and forays outside the recent price range looked unlikely, dealers said.
"Gold slowly drifted up yesterday, but it's just nearer the top of its range. There's supposed to be good selling just under $382," a London-based dealer said.
Bullion closed at $381.15 an ounce, a dollar above the Monday close but under the day's highsest price of $381.70.
Prices moved about a dollar higher overnight on buying in New York and Asia, dealers said. But the market was still fairly bearish and cautious more than a month into a steep price decline.
Gold was in the midst of a minor technical correction, with the target at $381.70, said analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse. Above that level, $384 should cap the rise.
"The upside at this point is limited and I still am quite bearish," she said. "The break lower last week below $378.40 does not leave this market looking very healthy," Jones said.
Silver ignored gold's progress and was unchanged from Monday's London close at $4.90 an ounce.
"Silver is lagging behind gold on this," a dealer said. "There's a real lack of any sort of demand."
Silver seemed comfortable for now within its $4.84-$4.95 range, dealers said.
But Jones of Credit Suisse noted that the recent range trading had a bearish feel to it because silver had made little attempt to break out towards $5.00.
Platinum was quiet at $384.50 an ounce, up just $0.10 from Monday's close. Platinum however, showed more scope than gold for a decent correction upwards, Jones said.
Its sister metal palladium was $1.25 lower at $118.25.

Traders in Tokyo said the chronic surplus in Japan's palladium market, which has depressed prices in recent months, would remain at least until the end of 1996 due to slack demand from the electronics industry.
